claude_proposed_widenings.name: triggered_ability_without_reaction_cost
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The current magic-item trigger-bound family requires consuming a Reaction. This item has a trigger-bound property that resolves on a failed save without spending a reaction, but still has its own dawn-based cooldown.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: If you fail a saving throw against an Enchantment spell that targets only you, you can turn your failed save into a successful one. You can't use this property of the staff again until the next dawn.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: modify_roll_substitute for spell_save_outcome_against_self
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Turning an already-resolved failed spell save into a success is an existing-v4-style roll/outcome substitution concept, but the current surface has no effect shape for replacing a save outcome after the trigger fires.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: If you fail a saving throw against an Enchantment spell that targets only you, you can turn your failed save into a successful one.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: reflect_triggering_spell
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The item needs to send the triggering spell back to its caster using the original spell context. The current surface can negate the triggering spell, but it cannot retarget or reflect that spell onto the original caster.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: If you succeed on a saving throw against an Enchantment spell that targets only you, you can take a Reaction to expend 1 charge from the staff and turn the spell back on its caster as if you had cast the spell.
